description: Start a cloud training job from an existing model or a base checkpoint (state-changing, may cost credits). Checkpoint mode is chosen by the model ref's shape and owner, not a list of model families: a name ending in .pt, or a model owned by another account (ul://owner/project/model or owner/project/model), is used as the base checkpoint, and the server decides whether it exists. Any other ref is one of your own models to retrain. Trains on exactly one dataset and requires epochs. The dataset is validated immediately, so an unusable dataset is rejected before any compute starts. In checkpoint mode a project model is created first, because starting requires a model id, so any rejection when training starts leaves that model behind, unrequested: a missing or not-ready dataset, an invalid gpu_type, a checkpoint/dataset task mismatch, or a 503 GPU_UNAVAILABLE when no GPU of the requested type is in stock, which is not a caller error (choose another gpu_type). The error names the model so it can be reviewed and deleted (models_delete) if unwanted. Starting is billable immediately: the platform has no cost preview before that, so the projected cost and remaining balance are only reported after the job starts. Training an existing model that already has a recorded run (any status past pending/untrained) replaces that model's status, epoch count, and training result history the instant the new job starts, and that history cannot be recovered afterward; the previously uploaded weights survive. That path requires confirm_history_loss=true in addition to confirm_cost=true. Checkpoint mode never destroys an existing model's history since it always creates a new one, so it never needs confirm_history_loss, including for another account's model — its own risk is the possible leftover model described above. An untrained or never-trained model needs no extra confirmation either. Use training_cancel to stop a job that is already running. Requires confirm_cost=true.

batch.description: Images per batch: -1 targets about 60% GPU memory, a value between 0 and 1 sets a memory fraction, and a positive integer fixes the image count.

confirm_cost.description: Must be true to allow a credit-costing training run. Starting is billable immediately; the platform has no cost preview before that, so the estimated cost and remaining balance are only reported after the job starts.

confirm_history_loss.description: Must be true to restart training on an existing model that already has a recorded run. Doing so replaces that model's status, epoch count, and training result history irrecoverably; the previously uploaded weights survive. Not required for an untrained model or for checkpoint mode, which creates a new model instead. Separate from confirm_cost.

dataset.description: Dataset ref by slug, owner/slug, or a ul://owner/datasets/slug URI.

epochs.description: Maximum full passes over the training set.

gpu_type.description: Cloud GPU type to allocate for training.

imgsz.description: Target input size: square batches normally, or the long-side size with rect=true.

model.description: Your own model to retrain (slug with project, owner/project/model, or ul://owner/project/model), or a base checkpoint: a .pt name such as yolo26n.pt or yolov5nu.pt, or another account's model such as ul://ultralytics/yolov5/yolov5nu (examples illustrative). Checkpoint mode auto-creates a project model.

project.description: Project ref that owns the training job and resolved model.

train_args.description: Additional YOLO training arguments passed through to the platform. epochs, imgsz, batch, and name here are silently overridden by the matching top-level input when both are set; data and model are rejected outright if present here.

name: training_start
